newsitem.title: USA: SoCal Edison nuclear unit seen up Saturday.
newsitem.headline: SoCal Edison nuclear unit seen up Saturday.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co expects the 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant to be restarted early Saturday, an Edison spokesman said Friday.

The unit was shut September 24 for unplanned repairs to stop a leak in the reactor's coolant system. It was initially expected to be out of service for two weeks, but the repairs took longer than anticipated.
The unit is "at full temperature and pressure, but is not yet on-line," the Edison spokesman noted.
After synchronizing to the regional power grid Saturday morning, the unit is expected to take 24 hours to reach full capacity.
The San Onofre's plant's other operating unit, the 1,070 MW unit 3, is scheduled to shut for a 70-day refueling on November 30.
Edison has a 75 percent stake in the nuclear plant, while San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and two municipal utilities share the remaining five percent.
